messages:
maya: Heads-up — I rolled the adaptive-merge heuristic to g4-pool @03:00 UTC (canary=10%). Dashboards show p50 for small requests (<=64 tokens) up by ~18ms right after deploy. Not a huge outage but noticeable for latencies that used to be 42ms -> now ~60ms.

leo: saw that spike, pinged infra. Also noticed a short dip in throughput during the same window. Might be queuing/backfill behavior.

sam: can you paste the deploy ID? I want to grep logs.

maya: deploy id: canary-merge-2026-11-04-0300. grabbing profiler snapshots now.

perf-bot: Automated alert: p50 latency increased 18ms for requests <=64 tokens on g4-pool between 03:01–03:06 UTC. Error rate unchanged.

leo: quick profiler snippet — tail of runtime log showed a flurry of microbatch merges followed by a few larger-than-usual kernel switches:
```
[03:01:14] batching: merged 7->12 in 6ms (token_budget target 48)
[03:01:14] kernel: selected nv_attention_v2 for shape (12, 64)
[03:01:14] kvcache: eviction probe triggered (hotset miss 0.12)
[03:01:14] queuer: backpressure hold 4ms
```

anya: that kvcache eviction probe stands out — when merge increases batch shape we sometimes probe a different KV alignment and touch slow-path. Could be padding/align mismatch causing an extra memcpy.

sam: I pulled a few perf traces. For merged batches the kernel selection path did an extra shape normalization step (`normalize_batch_shape`) which hits a slow path when `orig_seq_len` < 32 and we merged across hetero-lengths. Cost ~10–14ms per request in worst case.

leo: so two things compounding: extra shape normalization + uneven KV lookups after merge. That explains ~18ms. Any config toggles we can try short-term?

maya: I can revert the adaptive-merge policy to previous thresholds for the canary pool (set merge_min=3 -> 5, disable cross-length merging) if we want immediate rollback.

sam: before rollback, can we test a hotfix in canary: skip normalize_batch_shape when all orig_seq_len <= 32 or if merge_count < 4. Quick patch, low risk.

anya: also propose adding an alignment-aware memcpy for KV loads — the memcpy currently runs generic path for non-64-aligned offsets. That would be a bit larger change.

leo: agree we should try the quick skip first. If that fixes, we can land the memcpy/kv alignment work in the next sprint.

maya: patch deployed to canary (canary-merge-fix-1). Monitoring.

perf-bot: Canary metrics (03:08 UTC): p50 back to baseline within 90s of patch; throughput steady.

sam: saw the traces — extra normalize call skipped in the happy path, allocation churn down. Looks good.

maya: rolling the fix to 50% of g4-pool now.

leo: follow-up items: 1) add unit test for cross-length merge that verifies no extra normalize call, 2) KV alignment microbenchmark, 3) consider heuristic guardrails to avoid cross-length merging when estimated memcpy > threshold.

anya: I'll own the KV alignment microbenchmark and a small patch for memcpy fastpath. Will open PRs.

maya: thanks team. Filing a short postmortem note and adding the rollback/patch timeline to the release ticket.

sam: FYI — from the traces, kernel selection wasn't wrong, it was an extra prep step. Good catch.

leo: mark this resolved for now. Reopen if we see recurrence after full rollout. :thumbsup:
